selection_notes: Both identify Node 12 as a cytotoxic NK/CD8+ T-cell program mediating tumor-cell killing. C is more complete and directly connects the tree markers GNLY, GZMA, CD8B, and PRF1 to granule-mediated apoptosis.
answer: Primary Zone: Node 12 (Human_GNLY > 1,220 and Human_GZMA > 14,223 and Human_CD8B > 16,502 and Human_PRF1 > 17,449)Mechanistic Rationale:The pathway is consistent with cytotoxic cell activity leading to death of tumor cells.Cytotoxic cells such as NK cells and CD8+ T cells express perforin, granzyme, and granulysin proteins stored in lytic vesicles . Granzymes induce apoptosis through caspases , whereas granulysin causes pore formation in the plasma membrane . In addition, perforin creates pores in the cellular membranes of target cells, facilitating entry of the granzymes into the cytosol and endoplasmic reticulum . The resulting cell death leads to increased levels of CD48 and reduced levels of CD38, as observed in our pathway.Literature-Confirmed Findings• "Perforin-mediated killing of malignant melanoma cells requires the presence of both perforin and the pro-apoptotic protein, Bax" • "Granule exocytosis and target cell death were blocked by preincubation with anti-perforin antibodies." • "Perforinv1b-knockout mice developed solid tumors at a frequency of 40–100 percent over a period of six months."New Testable Mechanisms• Increased levels of perforin may lead to activation of NK cells against cancer cells.• Granulysin activates innate and adaptive immunity via the NLRP3 inflammasome.• Granulocyte macrophage colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF) promotes the release of perforine and granzyme from natural killer (NK) cells.Secondary Zone: Node18 (Human _NKG2D > 0,0776736 and Human_GNLY>1,205 and Human_CCL4 > 19,188)Mechanist Rationale:This pathway is supported by studies showing that NKG2C+ NK cells can recognize and kill human cancer stem cells (CSCs) through recognition of NKG ligands.In several types of tumors, such as lung adenocarcinomas, ovarian carcinomas, glioblastoma multiforme, breast cancers, and colorectal carcinomas , the overexpression of stress-induced self-ligands, such as ULBP1, MICA, and MICB, suggests that NK cells are able to detect and eliminate CSCs. For instance, NK cells could recognize and lyse leukemic stem cells (LSCs) using the NKG inhibitory receptor Killer-like receptor G1 (KIR2DL1) .Literature Confirmed Findings:• "NKG ligand expression is correlated with poor survival among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)" • "MICA/B upregulation increases susceptibility to NK cell mediated cytotoxicity" • "ULBP1 is associated with resistance to chemotherapy and worse patient outcomes"New Testable Hypothesis:• NKG cells can serve as potential targets for adoptive cell therapy to improve the efficacy of CAR-T cells in treating hematologic malignancies.• Expression of NK activating receptors can be enhanced by activators such as IL-15, zoledronate, and curcumin.
